title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): (S,τ) is a topological space, T⊂S is closed, U=S∖T, and τ'_0 is a topology on T finer than the induced one. The lemma says that among topologies on S finer than τ and inducing τ'_0 on T there is a coarsest one, τ'. Its closed sets are the X with three properties: X∩U is closed in U; X∩T is τ'_0-closed; and cl_τ(X∩U)∩T ⊂ X∩T.

This page:

(c) Restates (b) as a bijection. τ'-closed sets correspond one-to-one to pairs (B, A_U), where B⊂T is τ'_0-closed, A_U⊂U is closed for τ|U, and cl_τ(A_U)∩T ⊂ B. The correspondence is X ↦ (X∩T, X∩U). In modern terms this is the gluing (recollement) of an open piece U and a closed piece T along the 'closure' gluing map that τ already induces. The new topology keeps τ's gluing datum and only refines the closed stratum.

(d) Suppose τ and τ'_0 are 'ultra-topological', i.e. Alexandrov (arbitrary unions of closed sets are closed). Then τ' is also Alexandrov, and Grothendieck computes its specialization preorder. Here x ≤ y means x ∈ cl{y}, and closed sets are down-sets. The rule is:
- for x,y∈T, use τ'_0;
- for x,y∈U, use τ;
- for x∈T, y∈U, use τ.
The case x∈U, y∈T cannot occur because T is down-closed. Equivalently, for y∈U, x ≤_{τ'} y iff x ≤_τ y.

(e) Under (d), pass to the associated posets (T_0/Kolmogorov quotients) I, I' of (S,τ), (S,τ'). Let J⊂I be the closed down-set image of T, and let φ: I'→I be the canonical monotone map; set J'=φ^{-1}(J). He tries to describe the Alexandrov topology of the poset I' intrinsically, as the finest topology on I' that is finer than the pull-back (inverse-image) topology of I and induces a prescribed topology on J'. The sentence breaks off.

The next page lists conditions (i)-(iv) for this characterization, where (iv) asks that I carry the final topology for I'→I and J→I. That page then marks the attempt 'C'est faux' and refers forward to p.48.

Purpose: a dévissage / gluing lemma for refining a topology along a closed stratum, aimed at Alexandrov spaces, i.e. posets. This fits a chapter on an 'algebra of figures', presumably about stratified or combinatorial spaces described by posets.
errors: Parts (a)-(d) are correct. For (d), cl_τ(y)∩T is τ-closed in T, hence τ'_0-closed, so the τ'-closure of a point y∈U is cl_τ(y). That justifies the third case of the preorder.

The characterization in (e) is left incomplete on this page. The author himself declares it false on the next page ('C'est faux ... v. 48'), so (e) as written is an abandoned or incorrect formulation.

Minor: τ' is not literally a 'topology of I''. The intended object is the Kolmogorov quotient topology of τ' on I', compared with the inverse image of the topology of I under φ. The wording is muddled in the draft.

ideas.what: Coarsest topology finer than τ inducing a given finer topology on a closed subset; closed sets described by pairs (B, A_U) with cl(A_U)∩T⊂B
ideas.modern_name: Gluing / recollement of an open and a closed subspace (Artin gluing of spaces or locales) with modified closed part
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin–Grothendieck recollement of topoi (SGA4 Exp. IV, 9.5); Artin gluing of locales (Wraith, Johnstone)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. IV §9 (recollement of topoi); the point-set version here is not published as such

ideas.what: Alexandrov ('ultra-topological') spaces and their specialization preorder; preorder of the glued space computed piecewise
ideas.modern_name: Alexandrov topology ↔ preorder (specialization order); gluing of posets along a down-closed subset

ideas.what: Passing to T_0 quotients (posets) I, I' with the canonical map φ: I'→I and the closed down-set J; attempt to characterize I' as a 'gluing' with I as a final (pushout-like) topology
ideas.modern_name: Kolmogorov quotient; poset-stratified spaces; pushouts of Alexandrov spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; poset-stratified spaces in the modern sense (Lurie HA App. A, exit paths)

missed.claim: An intended intrinsic characterization of the refined poset I' over I, relative to the closed down-set J. It is abandoned as false on the next page with a forward reference to p.48.
missed.quote: la plus fine des top. sur I' qui induise sur J' la topologie T̄|J'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally: the problem is elementary combinatorics of Alexandrov spaces, and the correct statement is routine once posed.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct but elementary point-set lemma: a point-set shadow of open/closed recollement, specialized to Alexandrov spaces. The one non-routine attempt (e) is abandoned by the author himself. Nothing here seems absent from the literature in a way that would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The manuscript writes τ (tau), τ', τ'_0 throughout; the transcription's 𝒯, 𝒯', 𝒯'_0 denote these same topologies.
In d), 'T' aussi' is plausible: the manuscript reads 'τ' aussi' (τ' is also ultra-topological).

The bottom paragraph of e) begins with a struck-out word (possibly 'Alors'/'Mais'), then '{+si+} [-soit-] τ̄' est la top. de τ' déduite de τ' par passage au quotient'. The phrase 'relation d'ordre sur I' image inverse de τ̄' introduces τ̃ (the inverse-image topology), inserted above the line as 'soit plus fine que τ̃'.
